=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26718-26726, 31601-31622 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The wave check uses the integration PR head SHA captured in the external-finalize block at the start of the tick. Sub-issue merges later in the same tick (28129, 28869, 30080, 30144, 30476, 30625) move the head before `WAVE_COMPLETE` is recomputed (28564, 30812-30815), so the check classifies the old head.
  WHY: The pre-merge head classifies as green, so the clean-wave skip advances without inspecting the commit that holds the just-merged items, which defeats G9/D8. Severity disagreement: gemini says BLOCKER, minimax/luna/sonnet say MAJOR; the highest is used. sonnet raised this as a related item under its eager-final-PR finding.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26711-26726, 28580-28589 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The head SHA is captured only in the external-finalize block, which reads `final_merge_pr` before the eager final PR is created and recorded. On the tick that first records the eager PR, persist_orch_wave_check gives up with `reason=head_sha_unavailable` and fails open.
  WHY: For single-item wave 1 (the norm for phase-per-wave projects like #8427), the same tick sees `WAVE_COMPLETE=true`, so wave 1 always advances without its integration checks being read. Suggested fix: hold one tick instead of failing open.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:709-719 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: classify_check_runs blocks on every non-success completed check run, including advisory ones such as `copilot-pull-request-reviewer`. It ignores the `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` required-name set (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3052-3076).
  WHY: copilot fails on every PR with `custom_instructions_too_large`, so every wave boundary is classified red. With `FINAL_PR_PHASE_CAP_BYPASS` active, the judge then runs every tick, and long-running advisory checks hold the wave for 90 minutes before timing out.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:709-719 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: classify_check_runs collapses check runs by `name` alone and keeps only the highest-id run per name, ignoring workflow identity. A newer same-name success therefore hides an older failure or in-progress run.
  WHY: The classifier can return green while a real check is still red or running (this repo has three jobs named `lint`). This contradicts scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:202-206, which lets a newer run supersede only cancelled runs.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:707-708, 737-744 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `result["truncated"]` is computed, but the outcome ignores it. Green is decided from the first 100 runs only (`?per_page=100`, no `--paginate`, orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20099), and tests/test_persist_orchestrator.py:729-731 asserts green for the truncated case.
  WHY: A failing or pending run beyond page 1 is never examined, so the wave advances. sonnet raised this only as a hardening suggestion.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20160 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The Actions job-log request `{ gh_retry gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/jobs/${pwc_job}/logs" 2>/dev/null || true; }` omits `--allow-escape-sequences`. The repo uses that flag elsewhere (.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4650-4652).
  WHY: gh refuses logs that contain ANSI codes. `|| true` swallows the error, the log file stays empty, and the judge block says "(log unavailable)", so the planned 8 KiB log tail is lost. The mock gh_retry hides this in tests. Severity disagreement: sonnet/gemini/minimax say MAJOR, luna says NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:727-732 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The check-run id is stored as `log_job_id` and passed to the Actions job-logs endpoint (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20155-20160). The comment "For an Actions check run the check-run id is the job id." is claimed to be wrong (see scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:284-285).
  WHY: When the ids differ, the log request fails silently and the judge block loses the failure log tail. Disagreement: sonnet explicitly rejected this, saying the ids are the same for Actions check runs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20090-20095 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The scratch_unwritable path in persist_orch_wave_check returns 0 without clearing an existing `wave_check_wait_since` and leaves `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_HOLD=false`.
  WHY: The caller advances through the clean-wave skip, and a later held boundary inherits the stale timestamp, so it can time out early or immediately. Severity disagreement: gemini says MAJOR, minimax/luna say NIT; the highest is used. sonnet raised this only as a hardening suggestion.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20099, 20150-20160 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: When `PERSIST_JOURNAL_LOGIN_CACHE` is empty, a red or timeout result makes three GitHub reads per wave boundary: check-runs, `gh api user --jq .login`, and job logs.
  WHY: This exceeds P9's budget of "at most 2 calls per wave boundary per tick" and adds rate-limit pressure on repeated failing ticks. Severity disagreement: gemini/minimax say MAJOR, luna says NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20080 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `if [ ! -f scripts/persist_orchestrator.py ]; then` leaves the path argument unquoted.
  WHY: Claimed ShellCheck (SC2086) failure blocking CI and the release gate. Disagreement: sonnet rejected this, saying the literal path has nothing to quote.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20059-20083, 20130-20141, 20099-20111, 20006-20022 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `wave_check_wait_since` is a single timestamp with no head SHA or wave index attached, so the wait clock is not restarted when the integration PR head moves during a hold.
  WHY: A new head's fresh pending checks can time out early using the elapsed time of an older head's wait, which contradicts the agents.d fragment and the plan wording. sonnet raised this only as a hardening suggestion.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:766 | severity=high | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `max_wait = _env_hours("PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES", WAVE_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES_DEFAULT)` resolves a minutes variable through a helper whose name implies hours.
  WHY: If `_env_hours` really interprets the value as hours, the timeout fires after 90 hours. This is conditional and unverified against the `_env_hours` body.
- agents.d/8427-p9-persist-wave-check.md:(new 16-line fragment under "## Workflow architecture") | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new agents.d fragment is claimed to push the Copilot custom instructions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) past the size cap, causing `custom_instructions_too_large`.
  WHY: `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` then fails on every push and permanently blocks merge. Disagreement: sonnet rejected this, saying the fragment is not folded into the root AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md by this PR.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:756-771, 818-840 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `args.now` fails to parse, cmd_wave_check returns `outcome=error reason=args_invalid` without writing a result file; a `wave_index` parse failure falls back to -1.
  WHY: Reachable only with bogus args; the poller passes numeric values and the path fails open. The reviewer called it documentation-only and said to skip it.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The P9 deliverables and tests listed in the plan are implemented and pass." This implies registering the P9 phase label, following the P1-P8 convention.
  expected_change_site: scripts/label_helpers.sh (`_AI_PHASE_LABELS` array), .github/ai/label_contract.v1.json, tests/test_persist_postmerge_verify.py
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The CI failure in tests/test_persist_postmerge_verify.py::test_phase_labels_mirror_label_helpers_and_label_is_registered shows the P9 label (tracking issue #8427) is not registered. The diff touches neither scripts/label_helpers.sh nor .github/ai/label_contract.v1.json, and `_AI_PHASE_LABELS` and `ppv.PHASE_LABELS` in scripts/persist_postmerge_verify.py are unchanged. Disagreement: sonnet rejected this gap, saying the test reads only files this diff does not touch.
- requirement: The PR description lists "Failures caused by this change: 6" (tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py, tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py, tests/test_persist_postmerge_verify.py::test_phase_labels_mirror_label_helpers_and_label_is_registered, tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py, ruff, shellcheck). The acceptance criteria require the P9 tests to "pass".
  expected_change_site: scripts/persist_orchestrator.py and scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (ruff/shellcheck fixes, e.g. the unquoted `[ ! -f scripts/persist_orchestrator.py ]` at line 20080), plus whatever file each failing test exercises
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The diff has no ruff-fix or shellcheck-fix hunks in scripts/persist_orchestrator.py or scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, and the four named test files receive no hunks.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:classify_check_runs (`kept = [...] not in WAVE_CHECK_IGNORED_CONCLUSIONS`, `failing = [...]`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Every check run on the integration PR head blocks the wave, including advisory ones. The wave check ignores `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3052-3076).
  WHY: copilot `custom_instructions_too_large` makes every boundary red. `FINAL_PR_PHASE_CAP_BYPASS` (line 31684) skips the judge-cycle cap, so the judge runs every tick, and advisory checks such as `review / codex-agent` hold the wave for 90 minutes and then time out. Suggested fix: `--required-names` built from `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS`.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:classify_check_runs (the `newest: dict[str, dict]` loop) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Check runs are collapsed by name alone, which scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:202-206 says is unsafe.
  WHY: A newer same-name success hides a failure or an in-progress run, so the outcome is green and the wave advances. Suggested fix: let a newer run supersede only `cancelled` runs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26723-26726, 26711, 28580-28589 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: No head SHA is captured on the tick that first records the eager final PR, so persist_orch_wave_check fails open with `reason=head_sha_unavailable`.
  WHY: Single-item wave 1 always advances without its integration checks being read. Related: same-tick merges (28129, 28869, 30080, 30144, 30476) followed by the `WAVE_COMPLETE` recompute at 30812-30815 mean the check can classify the pre-merge head. Suggested fix: hold
